title: The Hijrah – from Makkah to Madinah
intro: The pledges of ‘Aqabah, the night the Prophet (SAW) left Makkah, the cave of Thawr – and the welcome in Madinah.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: If you do not help him, Allah already helped him when the disbelievers drove him out – the second of two, when they were both in the cave and he said to his companion: “Don’t be sad, Allah is with us.” Then Allah sent down His calm upon him and supported him with armies you did not see, and made the word of the disbelievers the lowest, while Allah’s word is the highest. Allah is Almighty and Wise. <small>(Qur’an, At-Tawbah 9:40, meaning)</small>

In the 11th year of prophethood (July 620), during the Hajj, the Prophet (SAW) met a group of people from Yathrib – the old name of Madinah. He used to talk with people who came for Hajj and invite them to Islam. That year, at ‘Aqabah, he met six respected men from Yathrib and asked them to sit with him for a short while. He recited some ayahs of the Qur’an and told them about Islam, and by Allah’s will they believed and accepted Islam.

items: The next year, 12 Muslims from Yathrib gave their pledge at ‘Aqabah. The Prophet (SAW) sent Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr with them to lead them in prayer and teach them Islam.
In the 13th year of prophethood, a group of 73 men and 2 women came to Makkah.

learn.html: After the pledge at ‘Aqabah, the people of Yathrib invited the Muslims of Makkah to move there, offering them the comfort and protection they did not have in Makkah. The Prophet (SAW) told the Muslims of Makkah to move to Yathrib, and they did, in small groups. They secretly left Makkah, leaving their families, houses and property behind. In their hearts they carried only their faith in Islam – and that was enough to give them strength to leave, for Allah’s pleasure, everything they had built over the years. After a few months, only Muhammad (SAW), his faithful friend Abu Bakr and his cousin ‘Ali (RA) were left in Makkah. The mushrikun noticed the Muslims were leaving, so they stopped them and tried to block the Hijrah.

The mushrikun watched the Prophet (SAW) and tried to stop him leaving. The council of the worst enemies of Islam met and decided to kill the Messenger of Allah: several young men would strike him at the same moment, so no one would know whose blow killed him. Allah (SWT) told His Messenger about their plan and allowed him to leave Makkah. Muhammad (SAW) agreed with Abu Bakr on the time to leave, and left his cousin ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib in his bed.

The Prophet (SAW) walked out of his house, which the mushrikun had surrounded, without being seen, and hid with Abu Bakr in the cave of Thawr. Searching for them, the mushrikun came right up to the entrance of the cave. Abu Bakr became worried for the safety of the Prophet (SAW), who noticed and told him not to be afraid. By Allah’s decree, a spider had spun its web across the entrance, and a dove had laid eggs in a nest there, which made the mushrikun think that no one had gone in for a long time – so they went back.

They stayed in the cave for three days, then set off to the place where a skilled desert guide, ‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit, was waiting with camels. On the way they were caught up by Suraqah ibn Malik, who wanted to bring Muhammad (SAW) back, dead or alive, to win the reward of a hundred camels promised by the mushrikun. The legs of Suraqah’s horse sank into the sand, and he had to beg Muhammad (SAW) for help, promising to turn back everyone searching for them in the desert. Muhammad (SAW) made dua to Allah, Suraqah was saved, and he kept his word.

The journey to Yathrib – about 480 km – was not easy at all: it went through the desert, in great heat. In 622, on the 12th of Rabi‘ al-Awwal of the first year of the Hijrah, Muhammad (SAW) and his faithful friend Abu Bakr reached Yathrib, and after the Prophet (SAW) arrived the city’s name was changed to Madinah. The people of Madinah welcomed the Messenger of Allah with great joy – everyone wanted him to be their guest.

But Muhammad (SAW) told them to let his camel go, because it had been commanded where to stop. The camel stopped on a piece of land where nothing had been built. When the Prophet (SAW) asked who owned it, he was told it belonged to two orphans; he called their guardian and agreed on a price. On that spot the Prophet’s Mosque was built. In his first months in Madinah he stayed in the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, and when his own house was built he moved into it and lived there for the rest of his life.

learn.text: What the Prophet’s arrival meant for Madinah

items: the mosque was built, and it became the centre of everything,
the long hostility between the tribes of Aws and Khazraj came to an end,
the Ansar (helpers of Madinah) and the Muhajirun (emigrants from Makkah) were made brothers,
the first constitution in the history of humankind was written – the Constitution of Madinah.

learn.text: Asma’ and ‘Abdullah – young people in the Hijrah

learn.html: Asma’ and ‘Abdullah were the children of Abu Bakr who helped Muhammad (SAW) and their father leave Makkah safely for Madinah. One evening, when it was dark, the Messenger of Allah knocked on the door of his best friend Abu Bakr and told him it was time for their Hijrah, and explained the plan – which needed the help of ‘Abdullah and Asma’.

The plan was: leave their houses, hide in the cave of Thawr and stay there until they saw how the mushrikun reacted. While they were in the cave, Asma’ had to bring them food in the dark until they left the cave – which put her life in great danger. ‘Abdullah had to move around Makkah, listen to the plans of the mushrikun, and every evening, when things were quiet, pass the news to Muhammad (SAW) and his father – also very dangerous.

learn.title: Brave Asma’
learn.html: When the mushrikun found out that the Prophet (SAW) had left Makkah, they guessed Abu Bakr was with him. They came to his house and asked Asma’ where her father was. She said she did not know. Angry at her answer, Abu Jahl slapped her so hard that her earring fell off. By acting like this, she kept secret where Muhammad (SAW) and Abu Bakr were staying in the cave of Thawr for three days.
The people of Madinah are remembered welcoming the Prophet (SAW) with this song:

learn.label: Verse 1
learn.ar: طَلَعَ الْبَدْرُ عَلَيْنَا مِنْ ثَنِيَّاتِ الْوَدَاعِ وَجَبَ الشُّكْرُ عَلَيْنَا مَا دَعَا لِلَّهِ دَاعِ
learn.tr: Tala‘al-badru ‘alaynaa, min thaniyyaatil-wadaa‘, wajabash-shukru ‘alaynaa, maa da‘aa lillaahi daa‘.
learn.en: The full moon has risen over us from the hills of Al-Wada‘. We must give thanks, as long as anyone calls to Allah.

learn.label: Verse 2
learn.ar: أَيُّهَا الْمَبْعُوثُ فِينَا جِئْتَ بِالْأَمْرِ الْمُطَاعِ جِئْتَ شَرَّفْتَ الْمَدِينَةَ مَرْحَبًا يَا خَيْرَ دَاعِ
learn.tr: Ayyuhal-mab‘oothu feenaa, ji’ta bil-amril-mutaa‘, ji’ta sharraftal-madeenah, marhaban yaa khayra daa‘.
learn.en: O you who were sent among us, you came with a command to be obeyed. You came and honoured Madinah – welcome, O best of those who call to Allah!

practice.title: The road to Madinah
practice.prompt: Put the events of the Hijrah in order.
items: Six men from Yathrib accept Islam at ‘Aqabah
Twelve Muslims give their pledge, and Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr goes with them
The Muslims of Makkah secretly move to Yathrib
The mushrikun plan to kill the Prophet (SAW)
The Prophet (SAW) and Abu Bakr hide in the cave of Thawr
Suraqah’s horse sinks into the sand

practice.title: Who helped?
pairs: The Prophet’s companion in the cave
Listened to the plans in Makkah

practice.title: What changed in Madinah?
practice.prompt: Tap what the Prophet’s arrival brought to Madinah, then tap Check.

options.text: The mosque was built as the centre of the community
The hostility between Aws and Khazraj ended
The Ansar and the Muhajirun became brothers
The Constitution of Madinah was written
The Muslims went back to live in Makkah straight away
options.why: The Muslims settled in Madinah – it became their new home.

options.text: The city kept the name Yathrib
options.why: After the Prophet (SAW) arrived, Yathrib was renamed Madinah.

questions.q: What was the old name of Madinah?
Who was sent to teach Islam in Yathrib?
In which cave did the Prophet (SAW) and Abu Bakr hide?
What made the mushrikun think no one was in the cave?
options: A spider’s web and a dove’s nest at the entrance

questions.q: How long did they stay in the cave?

practice.title: Questions and talk
prompts: ❓ What came before the Hijrah to Yathrib? What did the mushrikun plan for the Prophet (SAW), and what happened?
🗺️ Retell the Prophet’s journey from Makkah to Yathrib.
📅 In which year did the Hijrah happen, and what did it mean for Yathrib?
🧒 Asma’ and ‘Abdullah were young, but they helped the Hijrah bravely. How can young people help Islam today?
🗣️ Talk with your muallim: Muhammad (SAW) made the Muhajirun and the Ansar brothers. What did that mean for them, and how did they treat each other? What lessons can we take from it today?
